newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast Lt. crudes drift down, dealing light.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast Lt. crudes drift down, dealing light.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes drifted lower in dormant midday trade, in reaction to weaker prices for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude and light buying interest.
Fixed deals for Line 63 crude, whose shipments are constrained because of limited line space, remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under October WTI, with postings plus $1.00.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude were flat at $2.30 a barrel under WTI, with most refiners balanced for the month and traders leaving the market early for the weekend.
Rumors were afoot that an ANS deal got done at $2.25 a barrel under WTI.
Cash October WTI fell five cents to $23.35/23.45 a barrel Thursday, pressured by weaker product prices and NYMEX crude's expiration tonight.
Prices for California Kern River crude remained $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
